mcqs.q: Does the limit of f(x) as x approaches a have to equal f(a)?
options: Yes — 1 is the smallest prime number.
No — the limit can exist even if f(a) is undefined or different from the limit.
The limit is always just the value of f at that point — that's how you compute it.
Limits always equal zero unless the function is constant.
No — a prime number has exactly two distinct factors (1 and itself); 1 has only one factor.

mcqs.q: What does the graph of y = 1/x do as x approaches 0?
options: y equals 1 because the numerator stays the same.
Yes — 1 is the smallest prime number.
y equals 0 because dividing 1 by something small is small.
y goes to plus or minus infinity — the graph has a vertical asymptote at x = 0.
